why: The two statements differ in clause (5). B asks that four orbit spaces be metrizable: |A| (topology generated by NatOpenA), |B|, |E_B| and |P*E_B|, with no compatibility hypothesis. A states |A| metrizable only in theorem_19_8_6_hyp, under the added hypothesis IsCompatible, which the project shows is not implied by Definitions 19.8.4/19.8.5 (definition_19_8_4_without_compatible). A has no statement about |P*E_B| at all. Everything else in B follows from A: A_to_B_part, proved from theorem_19_8_6_one_four (no IsCompatible) and metrizableSpace_natTopEB, gives Γ̂ fully faithful, (1)–(4) with Kb = bundleG and Kh = bundleHat, and |B|, |E_B| metrizable; uniqueness in (3) uses the project lemma isStrongBundleIso_id_of_isStrongBundleIsoOn. B_to_A: A is about the project's particular structures bundleG, bundleHat and mulBundleG (B's Kb, Kh are existential and determined only up to isomorphism). A also contains the structure maps of M(Γ,Γ'): tgtGmap is a local isomorphism, invG an isomorphism, and unitG, mulG are strong bundle maps. B does not mention these.
overlap: HARNESS: the vocabulary definition Umap (used in B's statement) has value ⟨(m̂ h, p̄ h), mGmap_pbarMap h⟩, so any term about B reaches the item theorem mGmap_pbarMap. Plain rt_check of A_to_B_part therefore does not pass on that single name (recorded with #guard_msgs), and rt_check_soft does not apply because the use is direct, not through an auxiliary proof field. rt_check with mGmap_pbarMap removed from the list is OK. The statement of A itself mentions item theorems in proof positions (isLocalStrongBundleIso_pbar's type contains isStrongBundleMap_pbar), so the partial lemma takes the two conjuncts it uses as hypotheses rather than A. No direction was proved, so there is no rt_overlap.

main.note: The main conjunct gives (1)–(4) and |A|, |B| metrizable under IsCompatible. It has no |E_B| or |P*E_B|, and B lacks IsCompatible. Conversely it is about bundleG and bundleHat, which B's existential bundles do not determine.
